rationale: Requires verifying that message content arrives unchanged, which is data integrity.
Identity data and spending history must be kept from anyone except the authorised issuer, which is confidentiality.
Keeps serving while rejecting injection and brute-force floods from hostile clients, which is resistance to attack.
Mandatory periodic replacement of the sign-in secret before sign-in is a credential-based authentication requirement, with no attack or data protection stated.
Requires identifying the developer by biometric match before signing, which is authentication.
Managers must prove identity with a valid credential, which is authentication; no protection of information is stated.
Hash comparison to reveal alteration of an archived report is integrity verification.
Enforces a minimum strength for operator credentials, which relates to authentication credentials; no attack is mentioned.
Blocks outbound telemetry that would disclose source code against disclosure rules, preventing unauthorised disclosure.
Idle timeout closes the session so an abandoned session cannot be abused by an attacker, per the session-expiry rule.
Obfuscating strings and licence keys so they cannot be read from the binary protects them from disclosure.
Only users presenting a valid registered identity token may submit jobs, which is identity verification.
Separate read and write permissions per component limit who can view and who can change data.
Guests are limited to view-only and all insert, update and delete operations are blocked, restricting who can modify data.
Passport and payment details must have been protected against disclosure in transit or be discarded, which is confidentiality.
Limits exposure of patient fields to what each module needs and withholds the rest, restricting access to data.
An integrity mark lets later modification of the binary be detected.
Requires stored data to remain correct and consistent after each committed statement, which is data integrity.
Encrypted link protocol that prevents interception of content is confidentiality; no alteration detection is mentioned.
Digital signature check confirms the file came from an authorised consortium member (origin) and detects alteration, with no non-repudiation since the signer stays anonymous.
Flags images whose ownership mark was removed or changed, detecting alteration of the data.
Clearing memory with camera streams or credentials prevents disclosure of leftover content.
Only the forecast-editor role may create or change scenarios, restricting who can modify data.
Validates ranges and formats and rejects inconsistent records, ensuring accuracy and coherence of data.
Restricts to the data administrator who may change edit entitlements, limiting who can authorise modification of datasets.
Hash verification discards rule sets that do not match, detecting alteration; origin is not mentioned.
Requires time-limited identity confirmation with the owner before replacing the credential, which is identity verification.
Detecting reuse of a retired session token is replay detection, which is resistance.
Each developer must be identified by a distinct credential before jobs are accepted, which is authentication.
Commands executed exactly as specified is correctness, and the text does not say whether it concerns protection against unauthorised modification.
Node addresses and capacity are visible only to the administrator role, restricting who can read information.
A MAC over the balance-change history lets tampering be recognised, which is integrity.
Hash comparison rejects datasets that differ from the recorded value, detecting alteration.
Locks into a safe state on fault-injection manipulation, which is resistance to physical attack.
Format validation prevents malformed entries from corrupting stored records, protecting data integrity; no attack is named.
Salary figures must be recorded without unintended alteration of stored values, which is data integrity.
Reversal is accepted only if source and totals match the original load, protecting data consistency, while source matching might or might not be origin verification.
Verifies the employee's PIN against a stored value before access, which is authentication.
Verifies the analyst's X.509 certificate at sign-in and reuses that identity across tools, which is authentication.
